tools.name: batch
tools.description: Run commands in order, stopping at the first error. Each step is {command, params}: an engine command id (as list_commands lists them). A step may also name one of these tools with that tool's arguments as params, and runs the engine command it stands for: set_parameter (parameters.change; `value` or `expression`), list_commands (engine.commands, with `filter`), describe_command (engine.describe), execute ({command, params}), measure (inspect.measure), compare_picture (inspect.compare_picture, numbers only: no overlay PNG), inspect_design (document.inspect), undo, redo, export, save, open, new_design, crash_reports; screenshot, body_topology, batch and pending can't be steps. On an error the steps already run are undone (unless rollback: false), so the batch is all-or-nothing; the reply names the failing step (index from 0), its error, every result before it, whether the design really went back (rolled_back), the steps whose changes are in the design (applied) and those never sent (not_run). The usual way to build a part: sketch, draw, dimension, finish, extrude, fillet… in one call. Give `expect` {volume_mm3, tol, bodies, bbox} with the numbers you computed beforehand: after the last step the design is measured and compared, so no separate measure call is needed; a mismatch is flagged as an error naming it, and the design is kept as built.

coalesce_parameters.description: Set each run of consecutive plain parameter edits (parameters.change or set_parameter with a name and a value, or changes) together, rebuilding the design once for the run instead of once per edit; a run that is refused goes step by step, naming the refused step. Other steps still see the design up to date. Each step keeps its own result; the run is one undo step (default false)

expect.description: Check the design after the call against the numbers you computed: {volume_mm3?, tol? (relative, default 0.002), bodies?, bbox?: {min: [x,y,z], max: [x,y,z]} (each coordinate within 0.05 mm)}. The reply gains `expectation`: {ok, measured: {volume_mm3, bodies, bbox}, expected, mismatch: ["volume: measured X, expected Y (+Z %)", ...]}. A mismatch is a tool error that names it first; the design is kept as built, so inspect it and fix it or carry on

bbox.description: Bounding box of all bodies together, mm, each coordinate within 0.05 mm

volume_mm3.description: Total volume of the closed bodies, mm³

profile.description: Like timings, and each step's `profile`: {boolean_ms, tessellate_ms, other_ms}, its time in kernel booleans, in tessellation and the rest (default false)

rollback.description: Undo completed steps when one fails (default true)

timings.description: Add `timings`: [{index, command, ms}] for every step run (the failing one included) and `total_ms` (default false)

verbose.description: false: a compact reply. Feature steps leave out the full body list (created_bodies, changed_bodies and removed_bodies stay), sketch steps the ids they repeat outside `created` (default true)

tools.name: body_topology
tools.description: The edges (index, midpoint, length, endpoints) and faces (index, name, area, centroid, plane normal, a `point` that lies on the face, and for a cylindrical face its `cylinder`: origin, axis, radius) of a body. Use an edge midpoint as the [x,y,z] point that picks the edge for fillet and chamfer; a face's point or its name picks the face for the face commands. `faces: "cylinders"` lists only the cylindrical faces, as `cylinders`, with the halves the kernel splits one cylinder into merged: {radius, origin, axis, extent, names}, `extent` the [min, max] distance along `axis` from `origin` that the cylinder spans, and no edges. That is enough to check where every hole and boss is, at a fraction of the size.

faces.description: "all" (default): every edge and face. "cylinders": only the cylindrical faces, merged, with their extent along the axis, and no edges

tools.name: check_parameters
tools.description: Try parameter values without keeping them: set every parameter in `set` with one rebuild, report what `report` asks for, and put the design back exactly as it was (undo history included). `measure`: volume, bbox, bodies and faces per body as the measure tool reports them; `errors`: the features that fail or warn and the parameters that don't evaluate; `cylinders`: every cylindrical face as {body, radius, origin, axis, faces, name}, the halves the kernel splits one cylinder into merged (origin is the axis point closest to the world origin). The reply ends with `restored: true`; if the design could not be put back the call is an error with `restored: false` and the values still applied. An unknown parameter name is an error and nothing changes. Replaces the loop set_parameter, measure, body_topology, set_parameter back.

report.description: What to report: measure, cylinders, errors (default all three)

set.description: Values to try, by parameter name: a number (mm) or an expression ("140 mm", "wall * 2"), as set_parameter's `value`

tools.name: compare_picture
tools.description: Compare the model's outline with the part in a reference picture — a concept render, a product photo, one view off a design board. The model's outline is `inspect.silhouette` from `view` (default front), `camera` and `bodies`; the picture's part is found by growing the background in from the border, so a backdrop's gradual shading stays background. The compare is outline only: holes are not compared — both the picture's and the model's holes are filled. `reference` is a PNG or JPEG inside the server's folders. `crop_px` / `crop_fraction` take one view off a board: [x, y, w, h] in pixels or as fractions 0..1 of the picture; `part_fills_crop: true` says the crop box is the part itself, for a crop that tightly frames it. `fit` names the dimension the scale comes from ("width", "height", "both"; default "width") — one uniform scale, never stretched per axis; "both" scales by width and reports `aspect_mismatch` when the shapes differ. Returns as text the overlap (0..1) and the model's top, bottom, left and right edges against the picture's in mm at nine stations (positive where the model reaches past the picture), and as an image the overlay PNG: model red, picture blue.

bodies.description: Body names to outline (default: the visible bodies)

camera.description: Look from this camera instead: {target: [x,y,z], yaw, pitch, distance, fov?} (radians, mm; as view.apply). A photo taken in perspective gets an fov

crop_fraction.description: [x, y, w, h] as fractions 0..1 of the picture

fit.description: The dimension the one uniform scale comes from (default width); both scales by width and reports aspect_mismatch

reference.description: PNG or JPEG to match, inside the server's folders

rows.description: The model outline's height in pixels (default 240)

view.description: Standard view (front, top, right, iso, ...) the picture is seen from (default front)

tools.name: crash_reports
tools.description: SolidCraft's crash reports on this computer (the app's when connected to it). Without `id`: the list, newest first (id, kind, time, message, command, count, version, path, replayable). With `id`: the whole report: message, location, backtrace, app version and commit, system, the command that crashed and the recent ones, and design_path / replay_path when it can be replayed: `solidcraft-cli crashes replay <id>`, or `solidcraft-cli run <replay_path> --in <design_path>`. Reports never leave this computer.

id.description: A report id from the list

tools.name: describe_command
tools.description: One command's parameter docs and, for commands with a typed contract (every new command, and more of the older ones as they are converted), the JSON Schemas (2020-12) of its parameters (`input`) and of a successful result (`output`); null for the others.

tools.name: execute
tools.description: Run one command with JSON parameters, exactly as the toolbar, palette and scripts do. Never opens a dialog. Examples: sketch.create {plane: "XY"}; sketch.rectangle.two_point {p0: [0,0], p1: [40,30]}; sketch.circle.center {center: [20,15], radius: 5}; sketch.dimension {entities: [curve id], value: "width"}; sketch.finish {}; solid.extrude {distance: 20, operation: "cut"}; solid.fillet {edges: [[0,0,10]], radius: 3}; solid.box {length, width, height}. Lengths are mm; expressions may use parameters and units ("width / 2", "30 deg"). Returns the command's result; failures leave the design unchanged. Sketch commands that add geometry return created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what they added, stable and not reused after a delete (undo rewinds the counters with the design), usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.* and sketch.delete. Feature commands return the feature's id and name, every body (bodies) and the bodies the feature created, changed and removed (created_bodies, changed_bodies, removed_bodies). view.pick {pixels: [[x,y]…]} answers the body, face, exact world point, normal and depth under pixels of a screenshot (read-only; docs/control-protocol.md). `expect` {volume_mm3, tol, bodies, bbox} checks the design after the command (as `batch` does) and flags a mismatch.

expect.description: Check the design after the call against the numbers you computed: {volume_mm3?, tol? (relative, default 0.002), bodies?, bbox?: {min: [x,y,z], max: [x,y,z]} (each coordinate within 0.05 mm)}. The reply gains `expectation`: {ok, measured: {volume_mm3, bodies, bbox}, expected, mismatch: ["volume: measured X, expected Y (+Z %)", ...]}. A mismatch is a tool error that names it first; the design is kept as built, so inspect it and fix it or carry on

bbox.description: Bounding box of all bodies together, mm, each coordinate within 0.05 mm

volume_mm3.description: Total volume of the closed bodies, mm³

verbose.description: false: omit the full feature body list and sketch ids repeated outside `created`; keep created_bodies, changed_bodies and removed_bodies (default true)

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export bodies to STEP (.step/.stp), 3MF (.3mf), binary STL (.stl), ASCII STL (format stla) or OBJ. The format comes from the extension unless given. URDF (.urdf) exports the whole assembly for robot simulators: a link per component placement with mass and inertia, joints from the assembly's joints, and STL meshes in metres written next to it (docs/urdf.md); RViz needs mesh_prefix such as package://robot/meshes/.

bodies.description: Body names (default: all; not with urdf)

effort.description: urdf: joint effort limit, N or N m (default 1000)

mesh_prefix.description: urdf: put before each mesh file name (default: none, so relative to the .urdf)

velocity.description: urdf: joint velocity limit, m/s or rad/s (default 10)

tools.name: inspect_design
tools.description: The whole design: user parameters (expression, value, errors), the timeline (features with type, suppressed, rolled back, error, warning, timing), bodies (volume, area, centre of mass, bounding box, face/edge/vertex counts), sketches (curves with ids and coordinates, points, constraints, profiles, degrees of freedom, solve status), assembly joints (what each origin is attached to: occurrence, the feature, face, edge or sketch curve its face names refer to, whether it resolves and why not; `execute` `joint.inspect {joint}` gives one), the active sketch, selection and undo depth.

joints.description: Joint definitions as joint.inspect gives them, when the design has joints (default true)

sketches.description: Full sketch contents (default true; false = summary only)

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: The command catalog: id, label, toolbar tab/panel, shortcut, one-line parameter docs and whether the command is enabled right now. Ids are dotted and lower-case (solid.extrude, sketch.create, solid.fillet, sketch.inspect, timeline.rollback). Optional case-insensitive substring `filter` over id, label, tab and panel (not the parameter docs, so a command id finds that command rather than every command whose docs mention it).

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Volume (mm³), surface area (mm²), centre of mass, bounding box and face/edge/vertex counts of one body or all bodies, with totals. With `items` (one or two selections, as `execute` takes them: faces, edges, vertices, sketch curves, profiles): one item's length, area or position, a circle's, arc's or cylinder's `diameter` and `radius` (with `circumference`, or an arc's `arc_length` and `angle_deg`), a slot's `slot` sizes; two items' `min` and `max` distance and, where one is round, `center_distance` (centre to centre, or from its axis). `summary: true` keeps one short object per body (name, volume_mm3, bbox, faces, closed) and the total volume: enough to check a stage against the numbers you computed, at a fraction of the size.

items.description: One or two selections to measure instead of bodies, e.g. {"type": "face", "body": "Body1", "index": 3, "point": [x,y,z]}

names_only.description: Only each body's name (assembly occurrences included) and its definition's, without measuring (default false)

summary.description: Per body only name, volume_mm3, bbox {min, max}, faces and closed, and total.volume_mm3 (default false: the full reply)

tools.name: new_design
tools.description: Start a new, empty design (unsaved changes to the current one are discarded).

tools.name: open
tools.description: Open a .sc design file (or a .solidcraft one from an earlier release), a STEP file (.step/.stp: a new design whose bodies come from the file, as an Import base feature in a component named after the file; an assembly's parts become nested components) or a mesh (.3mf/.stl/.obj/.glb/.gltf: mesh bodies in such a component; a glTF file's nodes become nested components and its materials appearances); the result reports the component (id, component_name). Replaces the current design; insert into it instead with the file.insert_step (STEP) or file.insert_mesh (mesh) commands. A STEP file from a system that has Y up opens lying on its back: `up: "y"` turns its component a quarter turn about X (Y becomes Z). glTF is Y up, so it is turned by default (`up: "z"` keeps its axes). `names` picks what the bodies are named after when the solids' own names say nothing useful.

names.description: STEP, IGES, FreeCAD and Rhino. auto (default): keep meaningful solid names, replace placeholders with the nearest named product, else instance; solid: the solid's own name; product: the part's name; instance: the occurrence's name, else the product's

up.description: STEP and glTF only. z keeps the file's axes; y: the file has Y up, so its bodies are turned to stand Z up. Default: z for STEP, y for glTF

tools.name: pending
tools.description: Bridged to the app: the result of a request that was still running when its tool call returned (an error starting "still running:"). Waits for it up to 60 s: then its own result (or error), or done: false while it still runs (call again). pending: null when nothing is running. A request still running was not cancelled: don't send it again; other calls wait for it before they are sent.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change.

tools.name: running
tools.description: What the app is running or has queued right now, for every client: each request's connection and id, method, command id (a batch's step count), seconds since it arrived (running_s) and whether it still waits its turn (queued); `self` marks a request sent on the connection that asks. Answers at once, even while the app is busy, and never shows parameters. Ask it when a call timed out or the app seems slow, before sending a change again.

tools.name: save
tools.description: Save the design to `path` or its current file (a design opened as .solidcraft keeps that name). New designs are .sc files. The default is a design container; a .json path selects plain JSON. Set format to container or json to override the path. By default the path must lie in one of the agent's folders: the folder of a design opened or saved in this session (not its hidden files), SolidCraft's recovery folder, or a folder this server was started with `--allow-path DIR`. For a folder outside them, ask the user to add `--allow-path` and that folder to this server's arguments in their MCP client configuration.

format.description: Design encoding (default: JSON for .json, container otherwise)

path.description: Path to save to, e.g. part.sc (default: the current file)

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Render the design and return it as a PNG image. Headless: a CPU render of the model, fitted to the view. Connected to the app: a screenshot of the window (source "window", the default) or a render of the model with the app's camera (source "model"). Both show an active section (inspect.section) with its cut face capped. `view` first turns the camera to a standard view or a saved named view (view.save), `camera` to              any camera (as view.apply). `grid: false` and `axes: false` leave the ground grid (on Z 0) and the origin's axes out of a model render. A body whose appearance is see-through (appearance.assign with an `opacity` below 1) is drawn see-through, so what is inside it shows: that is how to look at the body a cut would remove inside the material it meets.

axes.description: false: leave the origin's three axes out of the render (see `grid`). Axes hidden with browser.visibility stay hidden

camera.description: Look from this camera instead: {target: [x,y,z], yaw, pitch, distance, fov?}                         (radians, mm; as view.save and view.apply)

grid.description: false: leave the ground grid out of the render. It lies on Z 0 and cuts through a part that straddles it. Model renders only: default true, or as the app shows it when connected; with `grid` or `axes` a connected screenshot is a model render, and source "window" is an error

height.description: Render height in pixels (model renders; default 600)

path.description: Also keep the PNG at this path

source.description: window = app screenshot, model = model render

view.description: Standard view (iso, home, front, back, top, bottom, left, right, fit) or the name of a saved named view                          (default: keep the current one; headless starts at iso)

width.description: Render width in pixels (model renders; default 960)

tools.name: set_parameter
tools.description: Create or change a user parameter and re-evaluate the timeline. `value` is a number (mm) or an expression ("40 mm", "width * 2", "30 deg"); `expression` is the same thing under the name the parameters.change command uses. Give one of the two (both only when they agree). Returns the new value, the features recomputed (`recomputed`), the features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused instead (`restored`, e.g. after setting a value back) and any features that now fail.

comment.description: Comment shown in the parameters table

expression.description: Same as `value` (the parameters.change name); give one of the two

unit.description: mm, deg or "" (unitless); default from the expression

value.description: Number or expression (or give it as `expression`)

tools.name: skill_reference
tools.description: Read a document of SolidCraft's bundled agent skills (solidcraft-modeling, solidcraft-mechanisms, solidcraft-editing, solidcraft-checking) from the copy built into SolidCraft. `file` defaults to reference.md; each skill also has SKILL.md. Unknown skills or files are refused with the available ones.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change to the design.
